note: A blues solo that follows the chords: the A minor pentatonic scale with C♯ added (scale-neck "add"), first sliding into C♯ over A7 on a solo-over play-along, then over a 12-bar backing track landing on D over D7 as well. The note outside the scale is named with what it is and why it works, the chords are chord tokens counted the long way once, every note named is lit, and the tempo is moves; the key stays, since the added note is a note name.

exercise.title: Solo with the 3rd of each chord
exercise.why: The minor pentatonic scale has no 3rd of A7 in it, so sliding into that one added note when A7 plays makes a blues solo follow the chords instead of sitting on top of them.

cells.text: {{chord:I7}} is the 1st chord of the blues in A, built on {{1}}, and {{chord:IV7}} is the 4th chord, built on {{4}}. The neck below has the notes of the A minor pentatonic scale, with the ringed {{b3}} and one added note, {{c-sharp}}. {{c-sharp}} is not in the scale: it is the 3rd of {{chord:I7}}, so it fits that chord.

Press Play below to start the backing track, and improvise with the notes of the scale. When {{chord:I7}} comes round, slide from {{b3}} up one fret into {{c-sharp}}.
Practice until the slide lands on {{c-sharp}} as {{chord:I7}} starts, not after it.

Press Play below to start the backing track: a 12-bar blues in A. When {{chord:IV7}} comes round, land on the ringed {{d}}, its root. When {{chord:I7}} comes back, slide into {{c-sharp}} again.
If you lose your place in the 12 bars, wait for the lit box to show {{chord:I7}} and start your next phrase there.
